newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Weaker rand seeing aiding S.African tariff reform.
newsitem.headline: Weaker rand seeing aiding S.African tariff reform.

text.p: The weaker rand provided scope for an accelerated tariff reform programme to minimise import prices for South African producers, finance department director general Maria Ramos said on Friday.

Briefing the parliamentary finance committee on the 1997/98 budget, Ramos said the trade and industry department was considering "compensatory tariff reductions to adjust for the depreciation of the currency, which had been more than what had been anticipated."
Ramos said that although last year's sharp slide in the rand -- it lost 29 percent of its value against the U.S. dollar -- had been difficult to deal with, it had not been entirely negative.

"The currency did have to depreciate. There were times when it did depreciate way beyond a level that we would require to get exports going. It was quite undervalued at times, but the depreciation of the currency did help to boost exports."
But the weaker rand had placed upward pressure on costs, pushing higher South Africa's expected average inflation rate this year to 8.5 percent.
Responding to concerns about the apparently low levels of capital expenditure provided for in the budget, Ramos said it was clear that there would be no job creation without such investment.
"Reprioritisation of government expenditure is difficult with the kind of budgetary process that we have in place and that we are in the course of changing," she said.

She agreed that government was not investing enough in fixed investment but said that it did not have the resources to make a meaningful impact on its own. It was therefore forming alliances with the private sector to accelerate capital expenditure.
